_comment: THE writing rules, as DATA. One source, read by the checker and cited by the asd-ste100 skill. Before this existed the same list was hand-copied into three places — check-prose.js, the skill's prose, and Jonathan's global CLAUDE.md — and they had already drifted: the checker did not know about 'honest', 'not just X but Y', or reflexive em-dash hedging, all of which he had explicitly banned. Rules are data; the checker is mechanism. Adding a word is an edit here, not a code change.
_source_of_truth: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md — 'Banned word matters and all LLM-tell vocabulary' plus the no-candor-disclaimers rule. When those disagree with this file, HIS file wins and this one gets corrected.
banned_phrases: at the end of the day

candor_disclaimers._why: Jonathan: every one of these implies the default is to guess or lie. Do the check silently and state the result.

self_referential._why: Never write a sentence about the document itself. 'Three asks and one question' was also stale by one question, which is what happens to a summary of a thing that changes.

label_fragment._why: No general fragment check: deciding whether an English sentence carries a finite verb needs a parser, and a word list gets it wrong — an earlier version flagged 'We recommend this option.' A checker that cries wolf gets ignored, which is worse than no checker. What IS detectable is the shape that caused the trouble: a short bold label standing in for a clause with the real sentence trailing after it.
